about: Santa Claws for a Cause is a Stark Parks evening at the Wildlife Conservation Center in Sippo Lake Park.
Families help Santa Claws deck the halls of the center and fill the critters' stockings.
Guests who wish to can bring a gift from the center's wish list and watch Santa hand special items to the wildlife ambassadors.
Kids spend time meeting the animals who live at the center.
At the Holly Hospital station, children become wildlife rehabbers and bring a stuffed animal in for a check up.
Live music plays through the evening while guests drink hot cocoa around the fire.
The program runs from 5:30 to 8 PM on Friday, December 4, and Stark Parks lists no registration requirement.
Donations to the center can be made through the Stark Parks giving page.

kids: Make a take home Christmas craft
Hear holiday music in the living room
site: Stewart Manor House, 13480 Congress Lake Ave
about: The Manor House Open House is the holiday kickoff at Quail Hollow Park in Hartville, planned around the historic Stewart Manor House.
It is organized with the Quail Hollow Volunteer Association and Stark Parks naturalists, so volunteers and park staff share the work.
Only the first floor is open, and it sparkles with lights and festive holiday decorations, including a decorated tree in the house.
Music plays in the living room while visitors wander through.
Stark Parks naturalists lead a make and take Christmas craft so kids leave with something to remember the afternoon.
The open house runs from 1 to 3 PM on Saturday, December 12, and pre-registration is not required, so families can arrive when it suits them.
Admission is cash only at the door, at $5 per person or $20 for a whole family, with children age 3 and under free.
All proceeds go to the Stewart Manor House, which makes the visit a small way to support the historic home.
The Quail Hollow Christmas Tea on December 2 and 5 at the same house is sold out for 2026, so the open house is the way to see the decorated rooms this season.

kids: Meet Old Saint Nick at storytime
about: Grinchmas is a Saturday afternoon of Seuss style mischief that Stark Parks puts together for families around Canton, with the whole program tucked inside the library building at the edge of the lake.
The theme is a simple one: grow your heart three sizes, the way the famous green grump eventually did.
Over two hours, kids move between Grinch-y games, hands on crafts and a handful of other activities planned by the park district staff.
At 2 PM sharp a fireplace storytime gathers everyone together, which makes it a good fit for younger children who like to sit and listen.
Old Saint Nick himself joins the story hour, so the afternoon includes a meet and greet with Santa without a separate line or visit.
A spot has to be reserved ahead of time, and sign-up has been open through Stark Library since November 2.
The program belongs to the Stark Parks December Fest calendar, a month long list of holiday and winter programs across the county.
Parents can plan around the 2 to 4 PM window on Saturday, December 12, and arrive with the reservation confirmation in hand.

The same Saturday also brings the Manor House Open House at Quail Hollow Park from 1 to 3 PM, so families in the Canton and Hartville area have two Stark Parks holiday programs to choose between that day.
Stark Parks keeps a printable December Fest calendar on its holiday page, listing every program from the Winter Photo Contest on December 1 to the winter open house on December 30.
Registration runs through the library, and the Grinchmas listing is on the Stark Library events calendar.

kids: Visit Santa before he heads north
about: Santa's Winter Workshop is the final Stark Parks Christmas program with Santa Claus before the holiday arrives, held on a weekday morning when school is out.
Stark Parks bills it as his last stop before he heads up north, so it works as a goodbye visit for kids who have been waiting all month.
Children spend the morning on a craft and a scavenger hunt that sends them looking around the building.
Christmas Bingo gets its own round, and a holiday cartoon plays on screen for anyone who needs a seat and a break.
Parents are reminded that kids should write a letter for Santa and bring it along to hand over in person.
Nobody needs to sign up in advance, which makes the morning easy to add to a school break schedule.
The visit runs from 10 AM to noon on Tuesday, December 22, three days before Christmas.
It sits near the end of the Stark Parks December Fest calendar, just ahead of the Adventure Kids winter open house on December 30.
That December 30 open house is for ages 3 to 9 and has animal encounters, a craft and an obstacle course, with no registration, for families who want a second outing during the break.
Earlier in the month, the Wildlife Conservation Center in Massillon hosts Santa Claws for a Cause on December 4 for a different kind of Santa visit, with the animal ambassadors.
Stark Parks also lists the Silver and Strings Trio holiday concert at Tam O'Shanter Park on December 20 at 2 PM, free to attend, for families who want a quieter outing earlier that week.
The Canton Federation of Musicians presents that concert in the Tam O'Shanter Park Clubhouse as part of its winter series.
Stark Parks hosts the workshop at its Sippo Lake Park campus in Canton, reached from 12th St NW.
Because the visit is a drop in, families can arrive at any point between 10 AM and noon and still take part in the craft and the scavenger hunt.
